text: The Consumer Protection Act 2019 replaced the Consumer Protection Act 1986. What is the main reason for this replacement?
options: To make the Act more consumer-friendly
To reduce the burden on the judiciary
To increase the jurisdiction of the Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions
To reduce the number of consumer courts
correctAnswer: To make the Act more consumer-friendly
explanation: The Consumer Protection Act 2019 was enacted to replace the Consumer Protection Act 1986. The main reason for this replacement is to make the Act more consumer-friendly. The new Act has several provisions that are more beneficial to consumers, such as the provision of compensation for harassment by a trader or service provider.

text: Which of the following is a right of a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act 2019?
options: The right to be heard
The right to be represented
The right to be compensated
All of the above
explanation: The Consumer Protection Act 2019 provides several rights to consumers, including the right to be heard, the right to be represented, and the right to be compensated. These rights are essential for protecting the interests of consumers and ensuring that they receive fair treatment.

text: What is the jurisdiction of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) under the Consumer Protection Act 2019?
options: Only cases involving a value of ₹1 crore or more
Only cases involving a value of ₹10 lakhs or more
Cases involving a value of ₹1 crore or more, and cases involving disputes between consumers and service providers
All cases involving consumers
correctAnswer: Cases involving a value of ₹1 crore or more, and cases involving disputes between consumers and service providers
explanation: The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) has jurisdiction over cases involving a value of ₹1 crore or more, and cases involving disputes between consumers and service providers. This includes cases involving products, services, and other consumer-related issues.

text: What is the role of the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum (DCDRF) under the Consumer Protection Act 2019?
options: To hear appeals from the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (SCDRC)
To hear cases involving a value of ₹1 crore or more
To hear cases involving consumers and traders within its jurisdiction
To hear cases involving consumers and service providers
correctAnswer: To hear cases involving consumers and traders within its jurisdiction
explanation: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum (DCDRF) has jurisdiction over cases involving consumers and traders within its district. It is the first level of consumer court and has the power to hear cases involving consumers and traders within its jurisdiction.
